name: analysis5
description: four independent log analyses, then their sum (real agent work; README Amendment A5)

steps.task: Read {evidence}/log_1.txt. Each line of the log is `<UTC timestamp> user=<id> action=<action> status=<ok|fail> ip=<ip>`. The file is in time order. Do not modify any file under the evidence folder. Count the distinct users that have three events with action=login and status=fail where the third such event is at most 600 seconds after the first (look at that user's failed logins in time order; other events in between do not matter). Report that count as the integer answer.

Read {evidence}/log_2.txt. Each line of the log is `<UTC timestamp> user=<id> action=<action> status=<ok|fail> ip=<ip>`. The file is in time order. Do not modify any file under the evidence folder. For each user count the events with action=download and status=ok. Report the largest of those per-user counts as the integer answer.

Read {evidence}/log_3.txt. Each line of the log is `<UTC timestamp> user=<id> action=<action> status=<ok|fail> ip=<ip>`. The file is in time order. Do not modify any file under the evidence folder. Count the distinct ip values that appear in at least one event with status=fail and also in at least one event with status=ok. Report that count as the integer answer.

Read {evidence}/log_4.txt. Each line of the log is `<UTC timestamp> user=<id> action=<action> status=<ok|fail> ip=<ip>`. The file is in time order. Do not modify any file under the evidence folder. Look only at the events of user=u03, in file order. Find the largest difference, in whole seconds, between the timestamps of two consecutive u03 events. Report that number of seconds as the integer answer.

Four colleagues each analysed one log. Their integer answers are recorded by the script: read them with `python3 {kit} outcome --run {run} --step T1` and the same command for T2, T3 and T4 (do not read the log files). Report as the integer answer the sum of the four answers.
